From 14e32321f3606e4b0970200b6e5e47ee6f1e6410 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Marios Pomonis <pomonis@google.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Dec 2019 12:47:43 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: x86: Refactor picdev_write() to prevent Spectre-v1/L1TF
 attacks

This fixes a Spectre-v1/L1TF vulnerability in picdev_write().
It replaces index computations based on the (attacked-controlled) port
number with constants through a minor refactoring.

Fixes: 85f455f7ddbe ("KVM: Add support for in-kernel PIC emulation")

Signed-off-by: Nick Finco <nifi@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Marios Pomonis <pomonis@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Honig <ahonig@google.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reviewed-by: Jim Mattson <jmattson@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/i8259.c b/arch/x86/kvm/i8259.c
index 8b38bb4868a6..629a09ca9860 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/i8259.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/i8259.c
@@ -460,10 +460,14 @@ static int picdev_write(struct kvm_pic *s,
 	switch (addr) {
 	case 0x20:
 	case 0x21:
+		pic_lock(s);
+		pic_ioport_write(&s->pics[0], addr, data);
+		pic_unlock(s);
+		break;
 	case 0xa0:
 	case 0xa1:
 		pic_lock(s);
-		pic_ioport_write(&s->pics[addr >> 7], addr, data);
+		pic_ioport_write(&s->pics[1], addr, data);
 		pic_unlock(s);
 		break;
 	case 0x4d0:
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/i8259.c`**
   - The `picdev_write` function has been modified to replace the computation of the index based on the `addr` parameter with constant values.
   - Specifically, for the cases `0x20` and `0x21`, the code now directly uses `s->pics[0]` instead of computing the index from `addr`.
   - For the cases `0xa0` and `0xa1`, the code now directly uses `s->pics[1]` instead of computing the index from `addr` using a bitwise operation (`addr >> 7`).
   - The locking mechanism (`pic_lock` and `pic_unlock`) has been added around the `pic_ioport_write` calls for the `0x20` and `0x21` cases to ensure thread safety.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in the `picdev_write` function are aimed at mitigating vulnerabilities related to Spectre-v1 and L1TF attacks by removing the dependency on the potentially controlled `addr` parameter for index calculations. 
- By using constant indices (`s->pics[0]` and `s->pics[1]`), the patch reduces the risk of an attacker manipulating the port number to gain unauthorized access or control over the system.
- The addition of locking around the write operations enhances the safety of concurrent access to the PIC (Programmable Interrupt Controller) emulation, ensuring that the modifications do not introduce race conditions.
